misconceptions.statement: Simple interest does not depend on how long the money is kept or borrowed.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on principal and rate, the 'visible' numbers, and treat time as just a label.
misconceptions.fix: Simple interest grows with time: double the years and the interest doubles, since SI = P x R x T / 100.

probe.question: What is the simple interest on Rs 2000 at 5% per year for 1 year, and for 3 years?

misconceptions.root_belief: only the main quantity matters, not duration

misconceptions.statement: The simple interest on a loan is the total money you pay back at the end.
misconceptions.why: The words interest and amount are used loosely in daily talk about money owed.
misconceptions.fix: Interest is only the extra money; the amount to repay is principal plus interest.

probe.question: Rs 1000 is borrowed at 10% simple interest per year for 2 years. How much must be repaid?

misconceptions.statement: Compound interest means the interest rate itself keeps increasing every year.
misconceptions.why: Students hear that money 'grows faster' and assume the rate rises, instead of seeing that the same rate applies to a growing balance.
misconceptions.fix: The rate stays the same. Interest is calculated each period on a bigger amount (principal plus earlier interest), so the rupee interest grows.

probe.question: Rs 1000 is invested at 10% per year compound interest. What rate applies in the second year?
probe.wrong_answer: More than 10%, because it is compound interest.

misconceptions.root_belief: Growth in interest amount means growth in rate

misconceptions.statement: Compound interest is always larger than simple interest, even for the first year.
misconceptions.why: Students overgeneralise 'CI beats SI' without noticing that no earlier interest exists in the first period.
misconceptions.fix: For the first period (one year with annual compounding) CI and SI are equal. CI becomes larger only from the second period onward.

probe.question: For Rs 2000 at 5% per year for 1 year, is CI more than SI?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, CI is more than SI even for one year.

misconceptions.root_belief: Compound always beats simple from the start

misconceptions.statement: For half-yearly compounding, you halve the rate but keep the number of years the same.
misconceptions.why: Students remember 'halve the rate' but forget that the number of periods doubles.
misconceptions.fix: Half-yearly compounding means 2 periods per year at half the annual rate, so n years gives 2n periods.

probe.question: Find the amount on Rs 1000 for 2 years at 10% per year compounded half-yearly. How many periods and what rate per period?

misconceptions.root_belief: Only the rate changes with compounding frequency

misconceptions.statement: For 6 months, you put T = 6 in the formula SI = PRT/100.
misconceptions.why: Students plug the number given without converting units, since the formula only shows 'T'.
misconceptions.fix: Rate is per year, so convert time to years: 6 months = 6/12 = 0.5 year before using the formula.

probe.question: Find SI on Rs 1000 at 10% per year for 6 months.

misconceptions.root_belief: Use time number as given, ignoring units

misconceptions.statement: A rate such as 2% means 2% per month unless it says per year.
misconceptions.why: Everyday talk of monthly money lenders' rates and monthly pocket-money or EMI payments makes students assume a monthly default.
misconceptions.fix: Unless stated otherwise, an interest rate in problems is per annum (per year). A monthly rate must be stated as 'per month'.

probe.question: Rs 5000 is lent at 2% simple interest. Time is 1 year. What is the interest, assuming the rate is per year?
probe.wrong_answer: Rs 1200, taking the rate as 2% per month.

misconceptions.root_belief: Rates default to the payment period

misconceptions.statement: An EMI is just the loan amount divided equally by the number of months.
misconceptions.why: Students think of repayment as splitting the borrowed sum evenly and ignore the interest.
misconceptions.fix: EMI includes interest as well as principal repayment, so it is more than loan amount divided by months.

probe.question: A Rs 1,20,000 loan is repaid in 12 EMIs with interest. Is each EMI exactly Rs 10,000?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, Rs 1,20,000 divided by 12 is Rs 10,000.

misconceptions.root_belief: Repayment equals principal split into parts

misconceptions.statement: A longer loan tenure means you pay less in total because each EMI is smaller.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the smaller monthly payment and overlook the extra months of interest.
misconceptions.fix: A longer tenure lowers each EMI but interest accrues for more months, so total interest paid is higher.

probe.question: Which costs less overall: a 5-year loan or a 10-year loan for the same amount at the same rate?
probe.wrong_answer: The 10-year loan, because the EMI is smaller.

misconceptions.root_belief: Smaller payment means lower total cost

misconceptions.statement: A flat rate of 8% and a reducing-balance rate of 8% cost the borrower the same.
misconceptions.why: Students see the same percentage and assume the same cost, overlooking what it is charged on.
misconceptions.fix: A flat rate charges interest on the original principal for the whole tenure, while reducing-balance interest is charged only on the outstanding balance. So a flat rate costs more; its effective rate is higher.

probe.question: Loan A is 8% flat and Loan B is 8% reducing balance, same amount and tenure. Which costs more?
probe.wrong_answer: Both cost the same because both are 8%.

misconceptions.root_belief: Same quoted percentage means same cost

misconceptions.statement: If the interest rate is low, the loan has no other costs to worry about.
misconceptions.why: Students treat the advertised interest rate as the entire price of the loan.
misconceptions.fix: Processing fees, late-payment charges and prepayment charges add to the cost. Compare the total cost, not just the interest rate.

probe.question: Bank A offers 9% with a 2% processing fee. Bank B offers 9.2% with no fee. Which is surely cheaper because of the lower rate?
probe.wrong_answer: Bank A, since 9% is lower than 9.2%.

misconceptions.root_belief: Interest rate alone defines loan cost

misconceptions.statement: A credit card's interest-free period applies even if you pay only part of the bill.
misconceptions.why: Students hear 'interest-free' and assume any payment within the period avoids interest.
misconceptions.fix: The interest-free period usually applies only when the full bill is paid by the due date. Otherwise interest is charged on the unpaid amount, often from the purchase date.

probe.question: You spent Rs 10,000 on a credit card and pay Rs 6,000 by the due date. Is the remaining Rs 4,000 free of interest?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, you paid within the interest-free period.

misconceptions.root_belief: Partial payment keeps the free period
